record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: Find an example of a 1-greedy basis that is not symmetric, where a normalized basis (x_n) is 1-greedy if for every x and every m the greedy m-term approximation G_m(x), formed from m coefficients of largest absolute value, satisfies ||x - G_m(x)|| <= inf{||x - sum_{j in Λ} α_j x_j|| : |Λ| = m, α_j in R}.

evidence.quote: Definition 14.1. A normalized basis (xn)∞ 1 for a Banach space X is called to be C-greedy (1 ≤ C < ∞) if kx − Gm(x)k ≤ C infn ||| x − X j∈Λ αjxj ||| : |Λ| = m, αj ∈ R o for each x ∈ X.
Problem 14.2. Find an example of a 1-greedy non-symmetric basis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$ and let $(x_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ be a normalized Schauder basis of $X$. For $x = \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n(x)\, x_n \in X$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, a greedy $m$-term approximation of $x$ is any partial sum
$$G_m(x) = \sum_{n \in \Lambda} a_n(x)\, x_n,$$
where $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{N}$ is a set of cardinality $m$ such that $|a_n(x)| \ge |a_k(x)|$ for every $n \in \Lambda$ and every $k \notin \Lambda$ (with ties broken arbitrarily). The basis $(x_n)$ is called $1$-greedy if for every $x \in X$ and every $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
$$\|x - G_m(x)\| \le \inf\Big\{\Big\|x - \sum_{j \in \Lambda} \alpha_j x_j\Big\| : \Lambda \subset \mathbb{N},\ |\Lambda| = m,\ \alpha_j \in \mathbb{R}\Big\}.$$
The basis $(x_n)$ is called symmetric if there exists a constant $C \ge 1$ such that for every permutation $\pi$ of $\mathbb{N}$, every choice of signs $\varepsilon_n \in \{-1,+1\}$, and every finitely supported sequence of scalars $(a_n)$,
$$\Big\|\sum_n a_n x_n\Big\| \le C\,\Big\|\sum_n \varepsilon_n a_n x_{\pi(n)}\Big\|.$$
Construct an example of a Banach space $X$ with a normalized Schauder basis $(x_n)$ that is $1$-greedy but not symmetric.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be solved. The 2024 survey "Twenty-five years of greedy bases" reports that Dilworth and collaborators constructed an isometrically greedy (i.e., 1-greedy) subsymmetric basis that fails to be symmetric, providing a direct example. Furthermore, isometrically greedy bases that are not even subsymmetric are known: the Haar system in $L_p$ for $p\in(1,2)\cup(2,\infty)$ admits an equivalent norm under which it becomes 1-greedy, while it is not subsymmetric (hence not symmetric).

status_evidence.title: Twenty-five years of greedy bases
status_evidence.snippet: There are isometrically greedy bases that are not subsymmetric ... the Haar system in L_p ...
status_evidence.claim: Examples of 1-greedy bases that are not subsymmetric (and therefore not symmetric) exist.

status_evidence.title: Isometric Renormings for Greedy Bases in Banach Spaces (arXiv:2603.21733)
status_evidence.snippet: the Lebesgue space L_p can be renormed so that the Haar system is isometrically greedy, isometrically bidemocratic, and lattice 1-unconditional; Dilworth et al. found an isometrically greedy subsymmetric basis that fails to be symmetric.
status_evidence.claim: A 1-greedy basis that is subsymmetric but not symmetric was constructed by Dilworth et al., and the Haar system in L_p admits a 1-greedy renorming.
